## Dry-channel positivity inside the implicit solve {#sec-ch08-vic}

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
- The vertical implicit solve can return a mass change that would take a cell dry-negative.
- Switch: none of its own; active with the implicit scheme of the time-integration chapter.
- The clamp is recorded in a per-step buffer, which the redo detector reads.
- The limiter of @sec-ch08-theta does not cover this: it acts on explicit transport only.
:::

Everything else in this chapter acts on explicit fluxes. The implicit correction of the time-integration chapter solves a
column and hands back a mass change that no face limiter has seen, and that change can exceed what a
cell holds. This section is the guard on that path.

### Derivation

There is nothing to derive; the mechanism is a clamp with a record. What matters for the reader is the
boundary of responsibility. The tracer limiter guarantees that *transport* cannot empty a cell, and that
guarantee is per stage, for the explicit flux divergence. The implicit solve runs afterwards, on the
same state, and its correction is outside that guarantee entirely. A cell that survived the explicit
stage can still be driven dry by the implicit one, and that is the gap this clamp covers.

`[C8]` makes that boundary measurable. Over two thousand columns the limited explicit update never goes
negative, worst exactly $0$; a conservative implicit redistribution applied to that same state drives a cell
dry in $1999$ of them, worst $-1.4$. The clamp that covers the gap invents up to $2.2$ of mass in one column,
which is why it is a clamp with a record rather than a conservative operation
[check `src/snapy_report/ch08/positivity_check.py`, output `src/snapy_report/ch08/positivity_check.out`].

### Numerical method

The buffer is registered at `_dry_clamp_step` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::reset >}}) and updated at
{{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.cpp ImplicitHydroImpl::forward_masked >}}, where it takes the running maximum of the clamp applied in
this step rather than a count. Storing a magnitude rather than a flag is what lets the redo detector
distinguish a round-off clamp from a real one.

It is read through the accessor at `dry_clamp_step` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitHydroImpl::dry_clamp_step >}}) and cleared between steps at
`reset_dry_clamp_step` ({{< code src/implicit/implicit_hydro.hpp ImplicitHydroImpl::reset_dry_clamp_step >}}), so the value a redo decision sees belongs to the step being
judged.

### Tests

No test in the repository isolates this clamp. It is written here from reading.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- The implicit path has no positivity guarantee, only this clamp and the redo detector it feeds.
:::

1. **Not ported.** This chapter's checks cover the explicit limiter and the floors. The implicit clamp
   is inside a solve this chapter does not reproduce, so its behaviour is recorded from the code.
2. **A magnitude, not a budget.** The buffer records the largest clamp of a step. How much mass the
   clamps created over a run is not tracked anywhere.
